beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The prophet Isaiah painted a strange, almost sad picture of his people. The truth of God, he said, had become to them like a book that is sealed shut — right there in their hands, and yet closed, its meaning locked away.

timing.text: The prophet Isaiah painted a strange, almost sad picture of his people.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine a precious book, clasped and sealed, that no one around can open. Everyone senses it matters. No one can get inside it. The words of heaven, sitting sealed in the middle of them.

timing.text: Imagine a precious book, clasped and sealed, that no one around can open.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So they carry it to their most educated man, the scholar everyone respects, and they say, please, read this for us. He turns it over in his hands, and has to admit the plain truth: he cannot. It is sealed.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed:

timing.text: And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed:

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then they hand it to a plain, unschooled man, hoping simple honesty might succeed where learning failed. But he only shakes his head kindly. Neither the wise nor the simple can open it on their own.

Wherefore the Lord said,

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:

timing.text: Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Isaiah saw the deeper trouble underneath. The people still said the right words and kept the outward forms, honouring God with their lips — but their hearts had quietly drifted far away, and their worship had shrunk to habits taught by men.

timing.text: Isaiah saw the deeper trouble underneath.
The people still said the right words and kept the outward forms, honouring God with their lips — but their hearts had quietly drifted far away, and their worship had shrunk to habits taught by men.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And no amount of human cleverness was going to fix that. The wisdom of the wise had run to the very end of itself. The experts had no key for a sealed book, or for a heart that had wandered off.

timing.text: And no amount of human cleverness was going to fix that.

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.

timing.text: Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So God promised to step in himself and do something marvellous — a genuine wonder. Not one more lecture from the learned, but an act of God that would open what men had sealed and reach hearts that had wandered.

timing.text: So God promised to step in himself and do something marvellous — a genuine wonder.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is the beautiful turn in this verse. When human wisdom hits its limit, God is only getting started. He is fond of marvellous works and wonders — the very things the experts said could not happen. So the only question is a hopeful one. When the wonder comes, will you be humble enough to receive it?
